questions.q: In PIM, what does an "eligible" role assignment actually mean for the principal holding it?
options: The role is permanently active and the principal holds it at all times
The principal can activate the role on demand, for a bounded window, without holding it continuously
The assignment is pending manager approval and grants no access yet
The role has been revoked and is awaiting reassignment
questions.explain: Eligible means the principal can activate the role when needed for a time-boxed window — the opposite of a standing, permanent (active) assignment.

questions.q: Which of these is a per-role activation setting in PIM, as opposed to an assignment-time setting?
options: Whether becoming eligible for the role requires approval
Whether eligible assignments expire after a fixed number of days
Which management group the role assignment inherits from
Whether activating the role requires a justification and a maximum activation duration
questions.explain: Justification and maximum activation duration are activation-time settings. Approval-to-become-eligible and expiration of eligible assignments are assignment-time settings instead.

questions.q: Where is PIM for Azure resource roles (like Owner or Contributor) configured, compared to PIM for Entra ID directory roles?
options: Separately, under Privileged Identity Management > Azure resources, per management group/subscription/resource group/resource scope
In the exact same blade as Entra ID directory roles, with no separate configuration needed
Only through Azure Policy assignments, since resource roles aren't part of PIM
Only through the classic Access control (IAM) blade, bypassing PIM entirely
questions.explain: PIM for Azure resource roles is a separate surface from PIM for Entra ID roles, configured per scope and inheriting downward the same way standard Azure RBAC does.

questions.q: What does a PIM access review catch that a one-time audit of current role holders does not?
options: It automatically rewrites custom role definitions to be more restrictive
It blocks all future eligible assignments from being created
It forces a recurring, reviewer-driven re-approval, catching eligible access left over from a finished project that nobody actively cancelled
It replaces the need for Conditional Access policies on privileged accounts
questions.explain: An access review is recurring and requires explicit re-approval of each eligible assignment, which surfaces stale access that a single point-in-time audit would simply report as "currently assigned."

questions.q: Why does a mature PIM configuration aim for almost nobody holding a permanent *active* assignment to Owner or Global Administrator?
options: Because active assignments are more expensive to license than eligible ones
Because Azure Policy cannot evaluate resources touched by an active assignment
Because active assignments cannot be combined with Conditional Access policies
Because a standing active assignment is a continuous liability regardless of whether it's ever misused, while an eligible assignment is only active for a bounded, audited window
questions.explain: The risk of a permanent active assignment exists at all times it's held, independent of misuse. Eligible assignments confine that exposure to short, justified, time-boxed activation windows.
